title: Morton Smith v. Western Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The complaint was sustained only as to procedure. The SJC did not disturb Presbytery’s reversal of its earlier finding that there was no strong presumption of guilt, but annulled Presbytery’s immediate declaration against Payne’s views and remanded for Presbytery either to commence judicial process or rescind its strong-presumption finding and drop the matter.
first_summary: Smith challenged Presbytery’s reversal of a finding that an elder’s race-and-IQ views did not create a strong presumption of guilt and its declaration that those views violated the Constitution and Christian liberty. The SJC deferred to Presbytery’s discretionary strong-presumption determination but held that it denied the elder due process by immediately judging his views without trial. It annulled the declaration and remanded for formal process or rescission of the strong-presumption finding.
summary: Smith challenged Presbytery’s reversal of a finding that an elder’s race-and-IQ views did not create a strong presumption of guilt and its immediate judgment against those views. The SJC upheld the reversal as a discretionary determination, without addressing its merits, but annulled the declaration against the views because a strong-presumption finding required judicial process. On remand, Presbytery was to commence process against the elder or rescind that finding and drop the matter. The ruling did not restrict Presbytery’s ability to adopt general position statements outside an investigation.
